From ee6e69d032550687a3422504bfca3f834c7b5061 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 18:22:53 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] iommupt: Fix short gather if the unmap goes into a large
 mapping

unmap has the odd behavior that it can unmap more than requested if the
ending point lands within the middle of a large or contiguous IOPTE.

In this case the gather should flush everything unmapped which can be
larger than what was requested to be unmapped. The gather was only
flushing the range requested to be unmapped, not extending to the extra
range, resulting in a short invalidation if the caller hits this special
condition.

This was found by the new invalidation/gather test I am adding in
preparation for ARMv8. Claude deduced the root cause.

As far as I remember nothing relies on unmapping a large entry, so this is
likely not a triggerable bug.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 7c53f4238aa8 ("iommupt: Add unmap_pages op")
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Samiullah Khawaja <skhawaja@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Vasant Hegde <vasant.hegde@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <joerg.roedel@amd.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h b/drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h
index 3e33fe64feab..7e7a6e7abdee 100644
--- a/drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h
+++ b/drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h
@@ -1057,7 +1057,7 @@ size_t DOMAIN_NS(unmap_pages)(struct iommu_domain *domain, unsigned long iova,
 
 	pt_walk_range(&range, __unmap_range, &unmap);
 
-	gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len,
+	gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, unmap.unmapped,
 			   &unmap.free_list);
 
 	return unmap.unmapped;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the `unmap_pages` function within `drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h`. The modification changes the `len` parameter passed to `gather_range_pages()` from the requested unmapped length (`len`) to the actual unmapped length (`unmap.unmapped`). This correction ensures that when the unmap operation extends beyond the requested range—due to landing in the middle of a large or contiguous IOPTE—the IOTLB invalidation gather covers the entire unmapped region, preventing a short invalidation. The change involves a single line in the file, maintaining consistency between the unmapped size used in the gather and the size returned by the function.

Here is the commit message:
iommupt: Fix short gather if the unmap goes into a large
 mapping

unmap has the odd behavior that it can unmap more than requested if the
ending point lands within the middle of a large or contiguous IOPTE.

In this case the gather should flush everything unmapped which can be
larger than what was requested to be unmapped. The gather was only
flushing the range requested to be unmapped, not extending to the extra
range, resulting in a short invalidation if the caller hits this special
condition.

This was found by the new invalidation/gather test I am adding in
preparation for ARMv8. Claude deduced the root cause.

As far as I remember nothing relies on unmapping a large entry, so this is
likely not a triggerable bug.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 7c53f4238aa8 ("iommupt: Add unmap_pages op")
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Samiullah Khawaja <skhawaja@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Vasant Hegde <vasant.hegde@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <joerg.roedel@amd.com>

Here is the root cause:
When unmapping a range that ends in the middle of a large or contiguous IOPTE, the unmap operation extends to cover the entire mapping beyond the requested length, but the IOTLB gather was only set for the originally requested length (`len`) instead of the actual unmapped length (`unmap.unmapped`), resulting in an incomplete invalidation.

Here is the patch:
 	pt_walk_range(&range, __unmap_range, &unmap);
 
-	gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len,
+	gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, unmap.unmapped,
 			   &unmap.free_list);

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len,
                   &unmap.free_list);
Reason:
The unmap operation may actually unmap more than the requested `len` when the IOVA range ends inside a large/contiguous IOPTE. This extended unmapping is recorded in `unmap.unmapped`, but the IOTLB gather was incorrectly limited to the original `len`, causing a short invalidation (the extra unmapped pages were not flushed from the IOTLB).

The code statements that fix the bug are:
gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, unmap.unmapped,
                   &unmap.free_list);
Reason:
Replacing `len` with `unmap.unmapped` ensures the gather includes all pages that were actually unmapped, even when the unmap extends beyond the originally requested size. This guarantees a complete IOTLB invalidation for the full unmapped range.
